- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1072` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +99
- **Deletions**: -12
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T14:56:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-29T21:12:22Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1072

## Verification of the report (against main `747424c`)

All three claims confirmed: `defaultBaseUrl()` returns full endpoint paths (`packages/fa_llm/lib/src/llm_config.dart`), the ollama-only `endsWith` fixup is the sole normalization, and `{PROVIDER}_BASE_PATH` / `{PROVIDER}_BASE_URL` appear nowhere in any doc. One scoping note: these env vars belong to `LlmConfig.fromEnvironment` in the `fa_llm` package — the `fa` CLI never reads them (its provider catalog resolves only `{PROVIDER}_API_KEY` via `lib/src/model_roles/provider_catalog.dart`), so the docs landed in the package README + dartdoc instead of `cli_help.dart`, where they would have documented vars the CLI ignores.

## Changes

1. **Uniform forgiving normalization** (`llm_config.dart`): every provider now accepts an origin (`http://127.0.0.1:8931`), a versioned base (`.../v1`), or the full endpoint (`.../v1/chat/completions`) and normalizes to the full endpoint the providers POST to — the `OPENAI_BASE_URL` convention of the OpenAI SDKs. Full-endpoint values pass through byte-identical (no behavior change for existing valid configs); an empty value stays empty so `ProviderFactory._effectiveBaseUrl` keeps its per-provider default fallback. This also fixes the ollama `.../v1` case that previously double-appended to `.../v1/v1/chat/completions`.
2. **Docs**: resolution order (explicit arg > `{PROVIDER}_BASE_PATH` > `{PROVIDER}_BASE_URL` > `.env` > default, `BASE_PATH` winning over `BASE_URL`) and the accepted base-URL shapes documented in the `LlmConfig` dartdoc and a new Configuration section in `packages/fa_llm/README.md` (with the env-var table the issue asked for). Also fixed the README usage example, which showed the origin+version shape and a non-existent `openaiProvider()` helper.
3. **No strict validation added** — the issue asks for documentation and forgiving semantics, and the normalization accepts every realistic recorder/gateway input; garbage just gets the route appended, matching the existing ollama behavior.

## Evidence

- `dart test test/llm_config_test.dart test/provider_factory_test.dart` in `packages/fa_llm`: 16/16 pass — 5 new tests (origin → route for openai/openrouter/ollama, versioned base → single append incl. the fixed ollama `.../v1` case, full endpoint byte-identical for all three providers, trailing-slash tolerance, empty override stays empty) plus the untouched factory suite pinning the old defaults.
- `dart analyze lib/src/llm_config.dart test/llm_config_test.dart`: no issues.
- No new dependencies; help text untouched (`cli_help_test.dart` not exercised — nothing it guards changed).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record

blocks.text:
# fa_llm

Reusable LLM provider adapters for Fa and related projects.

Pure Dart core: OpenAI-compatible, OpenRouter, Ollama, and configuration.

## Usage

```dart
import 'package:fa_llm/fa_llm.dart';

final provider = ProviderFactory.create(
  LlmConfig(
    providerName: 'openai',
    apiKey: '[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]',
    baseUrl: 'https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions',
    model: 'gpt-4o',
  ),
);
```

## Configuration

`LlmConfig.fromEnvironment()` resolves each value in order: the explicit
argument, then the `{PROVIDER}_…` environment variable, then the same name in
a project-root `.env` file, then the built-in default. `PROVIDER` is `OPENAI`
(the default), `OPENROUTER`, or `OLLAMA`.

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `{PROVIDER}_API_KEY` | API key |
| `{PROVIDER}_MODEL` | Model id |
| `{PROVIDER}_BASE_PATH` | Base URL — wins over `{PROVIDER}_BASE_URL` when both are set |
| `{PROVIDER}_BASE_URL` | Base URL (see below) |

A base URL may be an origin (`http://127.0.0.1:8931`), a versioned base
(`http://127.0.0.1:8931/v1`), or the full endpoint
(`https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions`); it is normalized to the full
chat-completions endpoint the providers POST to, so a local proxy (recorder,
gateway, cost tracker) can be pointed at with its origin alone.

## Features

- OpenAI-compatible streaming completions
- OpenRouter model routing
- Ollama local inference
- Provider configuration and resolution
- Token counting and context window management

### `fullEndpoint` function edge cases

```dart
String fullEndpoint(String url) {
  final base = url.replaceAll(RegExp(r'/+$'), '');
  if (base.endsWith('/chat/completions')) return base;
  if (base.endsWith('/v1')) return '$base/chat/completions';

- `'/v1'`? → `/v1/chat/completions` relative — Uri.parse in provider would handle as relative path. Garbage in garbage out; acceptable.

The PR claims "Full-endpoint values pass through byte-identical (no behavior change for existing valid configs)" — this is FALSE for full endpoints carrying a query string, and for non-`/v1`-suffixed custom paths.

With `?api-version=...` the URL still "contains" the full endpoint but the `endsWith` check fails. So existing Azure-style configs break silently (requests go to a nonsense URL). Silent breakage of a previously-working config = BLOCKING? Hmm. Let me weigh:

- Does the repo itself use fromEnvironment? No (tests only).
- Is fa_llm published? Yes, pub.dev, v0.2.0. External users exist (it's advertised in README for reuse).
- Azure OpenAI endpoints with query strings: `?api-version=` is THE canonical Azure pattern. The package targets OpenAI-compatible providers. A user with `OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://myresource.openai.azure.com/openai/deployments/gpt-4o/chat/completions?api-version=2024-10-21` in their `.env` — before: works; after: silently POSTs to `.../chat/completions?api-version=2024-10-21/v1/chat/completions` (or actually — hmm wait, `replaceAll(RegExp(r'/+$'), '')` doesn't strip anything; `endsWith('/chat/completions')` false since it ends with the version digits; `endsWith('/v1')` false; so appends → broken URL). The HTTP request would get a 404 and throw with the status in the message — loud-ish at runtime, not silent. But config that worked now breaks.

Given the pre-PR behavior for OPENAI was "no normalization at all" (use verbatim), the new aggressive normalization is a genuine backward-compatibility regression for:
1. Custom-path endpoints not ending in `/v1` or `/chat/completions` (e.g. Azure `.../openai/deployments/<d>/chat/completions` — wait that one ends with /chat/completions so it passes through fine, unless query string).
2. Query-string URLs (Azure `?api-version=`).
3. Endpoints like `https://gateway/api` that expect NO suffix appending (previously used verbatim).

The PR description itself acknowledges: "garbage just gets the route appended, matching the existing ollama behavior" — but for OPENAI/OPENROUTER this "garbage" category is NEW (previously passed through verbatim). The ollama behavior was already append-anything-not-full-endpoint. So openai/openrouter users with custom setups now change behavior.

The docs claim "no behavior change for existing valid configs" which is overstated. I'd rate the query-string/Azure case as IMPORTANT (real regression risk for a plausible existing config; repo itself unaffected). A cheap mitigation: also treat URLs containing a query component (or ending in `/chat/completions?...`) as pass-through, or check `endsWith` on the path part only. ## Automated Code Review — COMMENT

**Summary**: The PR delivers what issue #1072 asked for — documented `{PROVIDER}_*` env overrides and forgiving base-URL normalization — and the ollama `…/v1/v1/…` double-append fix is real (verified: 16/16 targeted and 81/81 package tests pass, `dart analyze` clean). Three important issues remain: the normalizer is provider-blind and breaks the `ProviderFactory` copilot branch (which appends its own paths), verbatim query-string (Azure-style `?api-version=`) / custom-path base URLs that worked before now get `/v1/chat/completions` appended, and this published-package behavior change ships without the version bump + CHANGELOG entry the repo convention requires (cf. commit 54333f60).

**Next Steps**:
1. Exempt `copilot` from `fullEndpoint()` normalization (or gate it on providers that POST the fixed route) + regression test
2. Pass through URLs containing `?`/`#`, or match on `Uri.parse(url).path` instead of the raw string; add a query-string test
3. Bump `packages/fa_llm/pubspec.yaml` and add a CHANGELOG entry for the behavior change
4. Optional: pin the documented `BASE_PATH` > `BASE_URL` ordering with an injectable-env test, complete the README env-var table (4 of 8 variables), and soften the "as `OPENAI_BASE_URL` means in the OpenAI SDKs" dartdoc claim (SDKs do not insert `/v1` for a bare origin)

---


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-29):

🚨 **IMPORTANT: normalization is provider-blind — it breaks the `copilot` branch of `ProviderFactory`**

The comment claims "normalize every provider the same way", but `copilot` does not POST to a fixed `/chat/completions` route that the base URL should be normalized into:

- `ProviderFactory.create` (packages/fa_llm/lib/src/provider_factory.dart, `_createCopilot`) passes `config.baseUrl` verbatim as `baseUrlOverride` to `copilotBaseUrl()`.
- `CopilotProvider` builds its request URLs as `baseUrl + '/chat/completions'` (packages/fa_llm/lib/src/copilot/copilot_provider.dart:152), so its base must stay an origin (`https://api.githubcopilot.com`).

Consequence of this change:

```dart
LlmConfig.fromEnvironment(provider: 'copilot', baseUrl: 'https://api.githubcopilot.com').baseUrl
// → 'https://api.githubcopilot.com/v1/chat/completions'
// CopilotProvider then POSTs to:
// https://api.githubcopilot.com/v1/chat/completions/chat/completions
```

The new dartdoc scopes `PROVIDER` to openai/openrouter/ollama, but the code applies normalization unconditionally, and `fromEnvironment(provider: 'copilot')` is a supported public path (the factory has a copilot branch; `providerPrefix` even maps copilot's env lookups). No in-repo consumer hits this today (`toLlmConfig()` constructs `LlmConfig` directly), which is why this is not BLOCKING.

Suggested fix: exempt `copilot` from the rewrite, e.g.

```dart
if (resolvedProvider != 'copilot' && resolvedBaseUrl.isNotEmpty) {
  resolvedBaseUrl = fullEndpoint(resolvedBaseUrl);
}
```

plus a regression test pinning that a copilot base URL passes through untouched.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-29):

🚨 **IMPORTANT: aggressive append breaks previously-working verbatim base URLs (query strings, custom paths)**

Before this PR, `openai`/`openrouter` base URLs were used **verbatim** (only `ollama` was rewritten). Now any value not ending in `/chat/completions` or `/v1` gets `/v1/chat/completions` appended. Two realistic existing-config classes regress:

1. **Query-string endpoints (Azure native style)** — this worked verbatim before:
   ```
   https://myres.openai.azure.com/openai/deployments/gpt-4o/chat/completions?api-version=2024-10-21
   ```
   `endsWith('/chat/completions')` is false because the string ends with the query, so this PR turns it into
   `...chat/completions?api-version=2024-10-21/v1/chat/completions` — a 404 against a config that used to work.
2. **Custom-path gateways** not ending in `/v1` (previously POSTed-to exactly as configured) now silently get `/v1/chat/completions` appended.

The PR description's claim "no behavior change for existing valid configs" only holds for values ending in `/chat/completions` or `/v1`.

Cheap hardening that keeps the documented forgiving semantics:

```dart
String fullEndpoint(String url) {
  if (url.contains('?') || url.contains('#')) return url; // full URL with query/fragment: pass through
  final base = url.replaceAll(RegExp(r'/+$'), '');
  ...
}
```

(or parse with `Uri.parse` and match on `path` instead of the raw string). At minimum, add a test documenting the chosen behavior for a query-string value.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-29):

🚨 **IMPORTANT: published-package behavior change without version bump or CHANGELOG entry**

This line changes the observable output of the public `LlmConfig.fromEnvironment` factory for every provider (normalization now applies to openai/openrouter too, not just ollama). `fa_llm` is published to pub.dev (`.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` publishes on `fa_llm-v*` tags), and the repo convention for `fa_llm` behavior/feature changes is to ship both together — see commit 54333f60, which bumped `pubspec.yaml` 0.1.0 → 0.2.0 and added the CHANGELOG section in the same commit.

This PR modifies behavior but touches neither:

- `packages/fa_llm/pubspec.yaml` — still `version: 0.2.0`
- `packages/fa_llm/CHANGELOG.md` — newest entry still `## 0.2.0 — 2026-08-28`

Without them, a future `fa_llm-v0.2.x` tag would republish the package with identical version metadata but different `fromEnvironment` behavior. Please bump (0.2.1 is fine — arguably 0.3.0 given the query-string pass-through regression risk in the sibling comment) and add a CHANGELOG entry describing the new accepted base-URL shapes.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-29):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the "as `OPENAI_BASE_URL` means in the OpenAI SDKs" claim is only partially accurate**

In the official OpenAI SDKs, `OPENAI_BASE_URL` is a **versioned base** and the SDK appends only `/chat/completions`; a bare origin yields `<origin>/chat/completions` (no `/v1` is inserted). This normalizer instead maps an origin to `<origin>/v1/chat/completions`.

That convention choice is fine (it matches vLLM/LiteLLM-style servers and the package's own defaults, which all carry `/v1`), but the doc sentence over-claims equivalence. Suggest wording like:

```dart
/// … so a local proxy can be pointed at with its origin alone — a
/// superset of the `OPENAI_BASE_URL` versioned-base convention in the
/// OpenAI SDKs.
```

so users porting a literal origin-shaped `OPENAI_BASE_URL` from an SDK setup are not surprised by the inserted `/v1`.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-29):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the env-var table the issue asked for lists only 4 of the 8 documented variables**

The `LlmConfig` dartdoc added in this PR enumerates eight variables: `{PROVIDER}_API_KEY`, `_MODEL`, `_BASE_PATH`, `_BASE_URL`, `_MAX_TOKENS`, `_CONTEXT_WINDOW`, `_TEMPERATURE`, `_MAX_TOKENS_PARAM_NAME`. The README table (the artifact issue #1072 asked for) stops at the first four, so a README-only reader has no way to discover that max-tokens/context-window/temperature are configurable via env.

Suggest completing the table:

## PR Description

Fixes #1072

## Verification of the report (against main `747424c`)

All three claims confirmed: `defaultBaseUrl()` returns full endpoint paths (`packages/fa_llm/lib/src/llm_config.dart`), the ollama-only `endsWith` fixup is the sole normalization, and `{PROVIDER}_BASE_PATH` / `{PROVIDER}_BASE_URL` appear nowhere in any doc. One scoping note: these env vars belong to `LlmConfig.fromEnvironment` in the `fa_llm` package — the `fa` CLI never reads them (its provider catalog resolves only `{PROVIDER}_API_KEY` via `lib/src/model_roles/provider_catalog.dart`), so the docs landed in the package README + dartdoc instead of `cli_help.dart`, where they would have documented vars the CLI ignores.

## Changes

1. **Uniform forgiving normalization** (`llm_config.dart`): every provider now accepts an origin (`http://127.0.0.1:8931`), a versioned base (`.../v1`), or the full endpoint (`.../v1/chat/completions`) and normalizes to the full endpoint the providers POST to — the `OPENAI_BASE_URL` convention of the OpenAI SDKs. Full-endpoint values pass through byte-identical (no behavior change for existing valid configs); an empty value stays empty so `ProviderFactory._effectiveBaseUrl` keeps its per-provider default fallback. This also fixes the ollama `.../v1` case that previously double-appended to `.../v1/v1/chat/completions`.
2. **Docs**: resolution order (explicit arg > `{PROVIDER}_BASE_PATH` > `{PROVIDER}_BASE_URL` > `.env` > default, `BASE_PATH` winning over `BASE_URL`) and the accepted base-URL shapes documented in the `LlmConfig` dartdoc and a new Configuration section in `packages/fa_llm/README.md` (with the env-var table the issue asked for). Also fixed the README usage example, which showed the origin+version shape and a non-existent `openaiProvider()` helper.
3. **No strict validation added** — the issue asks for documentation and forgiving semantics, and the normalization accepts every realistic recorder/gateway input; garbage just gets the route appended, matching the existing ollama behavior.

## Evidence

- `dart test test/llm_config_test.dart test/provider_factory_test.dart` in `packages/fa_llm`: 16/16 pass — 5 new tests (origin → route for openai/openrouter/ollama, versioned base → single append incl. the fixed ollama `.../v1` case, full endpoint byte-identical for all three providers, trailing-slash tolerance, empty override stays empty) plus the untouched factory suite pinning the old defaults.
- `dart analyze lib/src/llm_config.dart test/llm_config_test.dart`: no issues.
- No new dependencies; help text untouched (`cli_help_test.dart` not exercised — nothing it guards changed).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold

# fa_llm

Reusable LLM provider adapters for Fa and related projects.

Pure Dart core: OpenAI-compatible, OpenRouter, Ollama, and configuration.

## Usage

```dart
import 'package:fa_llm/fa_llm.dart';

final provider = ProviderFactory.create(
  LlmConfig(
    providerName: 'openai',
    apiKey: '[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]',
    baseUrl: 'https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions',
    model: 'gpt-4o',
  ),
);
```

## Configuration

`LlmConfig.fromEnvironment()` resolves each value in order: the explicit
argument, then the `{PROVIDER}_…` environment variable, then the same name in
a project-root `.env` file, then the built-in default. `PROVIDER` is `OPENAI`
(the default), `OPENROUTER`, or `OLLAMA`.

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `{PROVIDER}_API_KEY` | API key |
| `{PROVIDER}_MODEL` | Model id |
| `{PROVIDER}_BASE_PATH` | Base URL — wins over `{PROVIDER}_BASE_URL` when both are set |
| `{PROVIDER}_BASE_URL` | Base URL (see below) |

A base URL may be an origin (`http://127.0.0.1:8931`), a versioned base
(`http://127.0.0.1:8931/v1`), or the full endpoint
(`https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions`); it is normalized to the full
chat-completions endpoint the providers POST to, so a local proxy (recorder,
gateway, cost tracker) can be pointed at with its origin alone.

## Features

- OpenAI-compatible streaming completions
- OpenRouter model routing
- Ollama local inference
- Provider configuration and resolution
- Token counting and context window management

Confirmed:
- `CopilotProvider` builds URLs as `baseUrl + path` where path is presumably `/chat/completions`. So the Copilot base URL must be an origin like `https://api.githubcopilot.com`.
- `LlmConfig.fromEnvironment(provider: 'copilot', baseUrl: <origin>)` now normalizes to `<origin>/v1/chat/completions` — which would break Copilot if `fromEnvironment` were used with copilot + explicit baseUrl. But `providerPrefix` for copilot maps to OPENAI... wait no, `providerPrefix` is used only for env key lookup. The provider itself is passed through as `resolvedProvider`.

So `LlmConfig.fromEnvironment(provider: 'copilot', baseUrl: 'https://api.githubcopilot.com')` returns baseUrl = `https://api.githubcopilot.com/v1/chat/completions`, and then `ProviderFactory.create` passes that to `copilotBaseUrl(baseUrlOverride: ...)` → CopilotProvider gets `https://api.githubcopilot.com/v1/chat/completions` as base, then appends `/chat/completions` → `https://api.githubcopilot.com/v1/chat/completions/chat/completions`. Broken.

But is copilot + fromEnvironment a realistic combination? `fromEnvironment` is a public API of the published package. The dartdoc added by this PR says "A base URL — an explicit `baseUrl` argument or a `{PROVIDER}_BASE_PATH` / `{PROVIDER}_BASE_URL` value — may be an origin..." and claims providers POST to "the full chat-completions endpoint". For copilot that's not true — CopilotProvider builds `baseUrl + path` itself. So the doc + normalization introduced a latent inconsistency for the `copilot` provider: the doc says the normalization applies to `LlmConfig.fromEnvironment` regardless of provider (well, it says PROVIDER is OPENAI, OPENROUTER, or OLLAMA — the doc explicitly scopes PROVIDER to those three).

## 0.2.0 — 2026-08-28

- GitHub Copilot as a first-class provider: OAuth device-flow auth (request/poll with pending/slow_down/expired/denied semantics), GitHub-token-to-Copilot-token exchange with dead-token detection, and login resolution.
- CopilotTokenManager: cached short-lived Copilot tokens with proactive refresh (2 min before expiry), 30 s minimum exchange spacing, single-flight locking, and forced refresh (getAgain) for 401/403 retries.
- CopilotTokenStore abstraction with an in-memory implementation for tests and apps without a secure backend.
- CopilotProvider over /chat/completions: streaming SSE and complete responses, mandatory Copilot headers, per-request X-Initiator and Copilot-Vision-Request, cancel that stops emission immediately, refresh-once retry on 401/403, and listModels() parsing capabilities/limits/supported_endpoints.
- ProviderFactory copilot branch with accountType (individual/business/enterprise), explicit baseUrl override, and entry-name-scoped token store wiring.
- LlmConfig gains optional accountType and entryName fields.

🚨 **IMPORTANT: normalization is provider-blind — it breaks the `copilot` branch of `ProviderFactory`**

The comment claims "normalize every provider the same way", but `copilot` does not POST to a fixed `/chat/completions` route that the base URL should be normalized into:

- `ProviderFactory.create` (packages/fa_llm/lib/src/provider_factory.dart, `_createCopilot`) passes `config.baseUrl` verbatim as `baseUrlOverride` to `copilotBaseUrl()`.

  if (url.contains('?') || url.contains('#')) return url; // full URL with query/fragment: pass through
  final base = url.replaceAll(RegExp(r'/+$'), '');

## PR Description

Fixes #1072

## Verification of the report (against main `747424c`)

All three claims confirmed: `defaultBaseUrl()` returns full endpoint paths (`packages/fa_llm/lib/src/llm_config.dart`), the ollama-only `endsWith` fixup is the sole normalization, and `{PROVIDER}_BASE_PATH` / `{PROVIDER}_BASE_URL` appear nowhere in any doc. One scoping note: these env vars belong to `LlmConfig.fromEnvironment` in the `fa_llm` package — the `fa` CLI never reads them (its provider catalog resolves only `{PROVIDER}_API_KEY` via `lib/src/model_roles/provider_catalog.dart`), so the docs landed in the package README + dartdoc instead of `cli_help.dart`, where they would have documented vars the CLI ignores.

## Changes

1. **Uniform forgiving normalization** (`llm_config.dart`): every provider now accepts an origin (`http://127.0.0.1:8931`), a versioned base (`.../v1`), or the full endpoint (`.../v1/chat/completions`) and normalizes to the full endpoint the providers POST to — the `OPENAI_BASE_URL` convention of the OpenAI SDKs. Full-endpoint values pass through byte-identical (no behavior change for existing valid configs); an empty value stays empty so `ProviderFactory._effectiveBaseUrl` keeps its per-provider default fallback. This also fixes the ollama `.../v1` case that previously double-appended to `.../v1/v1/chat/completions`.
2. **Docs**: resolution order (explicit arg > `{PROVIDER}_BASE_PATH` > `{PROVIDER}_BASE_URL` > `.env` > default, `BASE_PATH` winning over `BASE_URL`) and the accepted base-URL shapes documented in the `LlmConfig` dartdoc and a new Configuration section in `packages/fa_llm/README.md` (with the env-var table the issue asked for). Also fixed the README usage example, which showed the origin+version shape and a non-existent `openaiProvider()` helper.
3. **No strict validation added** — the issue asks for documentation and forgiving semantics, and the normalization accepts every realistic recorder/gateway input; garbage just gets the route appended, matching the existing ollama behavior.

## Evidence

- `dart test test/llm_config_test.dart test/provider_factory_test.dart` in `packages/fa_llm`: 16/16 pass — 5 new tests (origin → route for openai/openrouter/ollama, versioned base → single append incl. the fixed ollama `.../v1` case, full endpoint byte-identical for all three providers, trailing-slash tolerance, empty override stays empty) plus the untouched factory suite pinning the old defaults.
- `dart analyze lib/src/llm_config.dart test/llm_config_test.dart`: no issues.
- No new dependencies; help text untouched (`cli_help_test.dart` not exercised — nothing it guards changed).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after

blocks.text:
# fa_llm

Reusable LLM provider adapters for Fa and related projects.

Pure Dart core: OpenAI-compatible, OpenRouter, Ollama, and configuration.

## Usage

```dart
import 'package:fa_llm/fa_llm.dart';

final provider = ProviderFactory.create(
  LlmConfig(
    providerName: 'openai',
    apiKey: '[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]',
    baseUrl: 'https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions',
    model: 'gpt-4o',
  ),
);
```

## Configuration

`LlmConfig.fromEnvironment()` resolves each value in order: the explicit
argument, then the `{PROVIDER}_…` environment variable, then the same name in
a project-root `.env` file, then the built-in default. `PROVIDER` is `OPENAI`
(the default), `OPENROUTER`, or `OLLAMA`.

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `{PROVIDER}_API_KEY` | API key |
| `{PROVIDER}_MODEL` | Model id |
| `{PROVIDER}_BASE_PATH` | Base URL — wins over `{PROVIDER}_BASE_URL` when both are set |
| `{PROVIDER}_BASE_URL` | Base URL (see below) |

A base URL may be an origin (`http://127.0.0.1:8931`), a versioned base
(`http://127.0.0.1:8931/v1`), or the full endpoint
(`https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions`); it is normalized to the full
chat-completions endpoint the providers POST to, so a local proxy (recorder,
gateway, cost tracker) can be pointed at with its origin alone.

## Features

- OpenAI-compatible streaming completions
- OpenRouter model routing
- Ollama local inference
- Provider configuration and resolution
- Token counting and context window management

## 0.2.0 — 2026-08-28

- GitHub Copilot as a first-class provider: OAuth device-flow auth (request/poll with pending/slow_down/expired/denied semantics), GitHub-token-to-Copilot-token exchange with dead-token detection, and login resolution.
- CopilotTokenManager: cached short-lived Copilot tokens with proactive refresh (2 min before expiry), 30 s minimum exchange spacing, single-flight locking, and forced refresh (getAgain) for 401/403 retries.

- ProviderFactory copilot branch with accountType (individual/business/enterprise), explicit baseUrl override, and entry-name-scoped token store wiring.
- LlmConfig gains optional accountType and entryName fields.

```dart
String fullEndpoint(String url) {
  final base = url.replaceAll(RegExp(r'/+$'), '');

With `?api-version=...` the URL still "contains" the full endpoint but the `endsWith` check fails. So existing Azure-style configs break silently (requests go to a nonsense URL). Silent breakage of a previously-working config = BLOCKING? Hmm. Let me weigh:

- Does the repo itself use fromEnvironment? No (tests only).
- Is fa_llm published? Yes, pub.dev, v0.2.0. External users exist (it's advertised in README for reuse).
- Azure OpenAI endpoints with query strings: `?api-version=` is THE canonical Azure pattern. The package targets OpenAI-compatible providers. A user with `OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://myresource.openai.azure.com/openai/deployments/gpt-4o/chat/completions?api-version=2024-10-21` in their `.env` — before: works; after: silently POSTs to `.../chat/completions?api-version=2024-10-21/v1/chat/completions` (or actually — hmm wait, `replaceAll(RegExp(r'/+$'), '')` doesn't strip anything; `endsWith('/chat/completions')` false since it ends with the version digits; `endsWith('/v1')` false; so appends → broken URL). 1. Custom-path endpoints not ending in `/v1` or `/chat/completions` (e.g. Azure `.../openai/deployments/<d>/chat/completions` — wait that one ends with /chat/completions so it passes through fine, unless query string).

**Summary**: The PR delivers what issue #1072 asked for — documented `{PROVIDER}_*` env overrides and forgiving base-URL normalization — and the ollama `…/v1/v1/…` double-append fix is real (verified: 16/16 targeted and 81/81 package tests pass, `dart analyze` clean). Three important issues remain: the normalizer is provider-blind and breaks the `ProviderFactory` copilot branch (which appends its own paths), verbatim query-string (Azure-style `?api-version=`) / custom-path base URLs that worked before now get `/v1/chat/completions` appended, and this published-package behavior change ships without the version bump + CHANGELOG entry the repo convention requires (cf. commit 54333f60).

**Next Steps**:
1. Exempt `copilot` from `fullEndpoint()` normalization (or gate it on providers that POST the fixed route) + regression test
2. Pass through URLs containing `?`/`#`, or match on `Uri.parse(url).path` instead of the raw string; add a query-string test
3. Bump `packages/fa_llm/pubspec.yaml` and add a CHANGELOG entry for the behavior change
4. Optional: pin the documented `BASE_PATH` > `BASE_URL` ordering with an injectable-env test, complete the README env-var table (4 of 8 variables), and soften the "as `OPENAI_BASE_URL` means in the OpenAI SDKs" dartdoc claim (SDKs do not insert `/v1` for a bare origin)

Notes outside the diff (no action required for this PR): the default endpoint URLs are duplicated between `LlmConfig.fromEnvironment`'s `defaultBaseUrl()` and `ProviderFactory._effectiveBaseUrl` — worth consolidating next time either changes; and `dotenv_loader.dart` does not strip quotes from `.env` values, which composes badly with any quoted `*_BASE_URL` value.

---


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-29):

🚨 **IMPORTANT: normalization is provider-blind — it breaks the `copilot` branch of `ProviderFactory`**

The comment claims "normalize every provider the same way", but `copilot` does not POST to a fixed `/chat/completions` route that the base URL should be normalized into:

- `ProviderFactory.create` (packages/fa_llm/lib/src/provider_factory.dart, `_createCopilot`) passes `config.baseUrl` verbatim as `baseUrlOverride` to `copilotBaseUrl()`.
- `CopilotProvider` builds its request URLs as `baseUrl + '/chat/completions'` (packages/fa_llm/lib/src/copilot/copilot_provider.dart:152), so its base must stay an origin (`https://api.githubcopilot.com`).

Consequence of this change:

```dart
LlmConfig.fromEnvironment(provider: 'copilot', baseUrl: 'https://api.githubcopilot.com').baseUrl
// → 'https://api.githubcopilot.com/v1/chat/completions'
// CopilotProvider then POSTs to:
// https://api.githubcopilot.com/v1/chat/completions/chat/completions
```

The new dartdoc scopes `PROVIDER` to openai/openrouter/ollama, but the code applies normalization unconditionally, and `fromEnvironment(provider: 'copilot')` is a supported public path (the factory has a copilot branch; `providerPrefix` even maps copilot's env lookups). No in-repo consumer hits this today (`toLlmConfig()` constructs `LlmConfig` directly), which is why this is not BLOCKING.

Suggested fix: exempt `copilot` from the rewrite, e.g.

```dart
if (resolvedProvider != 'copilot' && resolvedBaseUrl.isNotEmpty) {
  resolvedBaseUrl = fullEndpoint(resolvedBaseUrl);
}
```

plus a regression test pinning that a copilot base URL passes through untouched.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-29):

🚨 **IMPORTANT: aggressive append breaks previously-working verbatim base URLs (query strings, custom paths)**

Before this PR, `openai`/`openrouter` base URLs were used **verbatim** (only `ollama` was rewritten). Now any value not ending in `/chat/completions` or `/v1` gets `/v1/chat/completions` appended. Two realistic existing-config classes regress:

1. **Query-string endpoints (Azure native style)** — this worked verbatim before:

   https://myres.openai.azure.com/openai/deployments/gpt-4o/chat/completions?api-version=2024-10-21

2. **Custom-path gateways** not ending in `/v1` (previously POSTed-to exactly as configured) now silently get `/v1/chat/completions` appended.

The PR description's claim "no behavior change for existing valid configs" only holds for values ending in `/chat/completions` or `/v1`.

```dart
String fullEndpoint(String url) {
  if (url.contains('?') || url.contains('#')) return url; // full URL with query/fragment: pass through
  final base = url.replaceAll(RegExp(r'/+$'), '');
  ...
}

The truncated diff actually covers nearly everything (only ~31 chars omitted in the middle — the pubspec repository/homepage lines). Let me now verify against the actual git diff for completeness, then deep-review the new `fullEndpoint` implementation.

New `fullEndpoint`:
```dart
String fullEndpoint(String url) {
  final uri = Uri.tryParse(url);
  if (uri == null || uri.hasQuery || uri.hasFragment) return url;
  final base = url.replaceAll(RegExp(r'/+$'), '');
  if (base.endsWith('/chat/completions')) return base;
  if (base.endsWith('/v1')) return '$base/chat/completions';
  if (uri.path.isEmpty || uri.path == '/') {
    return '$base/v1/chat/completions';
  }
  return url;
}
```

Analysis of the new logic:

1. `Uri.tryParse(url)` null → return url verbatim. Good.
2. `uri.hasQuery || uri.hasFragment` → verbatim. Good (fixes Azure).
3. Trailing-slash strip.
4. `/chat/completions` → pass. Good.
5. `/v1` → append route. Good.
6. **NEW**: if `uri.path.isEmpty || uri.path == '/'` → append `/v1/chat/completions` (origin case). 
7. **Otherwise (custom path)** → `return url` verbatim.

Wait — there are subtle issues here:

**Issue A: trailing-slash stripping no longer applied in the verbatim branches.** If url = `'https://gw.example/corp-route/'` (custom path with trailing slash) → not origin (path = `/corp-route/`), not `/v1`, not `/chat/completions` → `return url` — WITH the trailing slash, verbatim. That's fine per "passes through verbatim".

But `'https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions///'`? → base strips trailing slashes → endsWith `/chat/completions` → returns STRIPPED base `'https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions'`. OK — normalized (slash strip). The doc says full endpoints "pass through verbatim" — with trailing slashes they're normalized. Minor; the test only covers `.../v1/`. Fine, that's the previous behavior, consistent.

**Issue B: `'http://127.0.0.1:8931'` (origin) — `uri.path`**: For `'http://127.0.0.1:8931'`, `Uri.parse` gives `path == ''` → origin branch → append. Good. For `'http://127.0.0.1:8931/'` → path == '/' → append. Good — trailing slashes stripped by `base` first, then append: `'http://127.0.0.1:8931' + '/v1/chat/completions'`. Good.

**Issue C: What about `uri.path` for URLs with a port but empty host? Not realistic.

**Issue D: IPv6**: `'http://[::1]:11434'` — Uri.tryParse handles brackets; path '' → append → `'http://[::1]:11434/v1/chat/completions'`. Good.

**Issue E: The custom-path verbatim return changed semantics vs my round-1 suggestion**: my suggested "custom-path gateways now silently get /v1/chat/completions appended" — the author chose verbatim pass-through for custom paths. That's the SAFEST choice (byte-identical to pre-PR behavior for openai/openrouter). 

**Issue F — regression re-introduced? `ollama` custom-path**: pre-PR, ollama rewrote EVERYTHING non-full-endpoint (append `/v1/chat/completions`); post-PR, ollama custom paths pass verbatim. That's a behavior change for ollama custom-path configs — but it's the fix direction the issue asked for and matches openai. Fine.

**Issue G — `/v1` check happens BEFORE the path check**: url `'https://gw.example/corp-route/v1'` → endsWith `/v1` → `'https://gw.example/corp-route/v1/chat/completions'`. Hmm — is that right? A custom path ending in `/v1` gains the route. That's the "versioned base" semantics — any path ending `/v1` is treated as versioned base. Reasonable and consistent with docs ("a versioned base (`http://127.0.0.1:8931/v1`)"). Fine.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger …

blocks.text:
# fa_llm

Reusable LLM provider adapters for Fa and related projects.

Pure Dart core: OpenAI-compatible, OpenRouter, Ollama, and configuration.

## Usage

```dart
import 'package:fa_llm/fa_llm.dart';

final provider = ProviderFactory.create(
  LlmConfig(
    providerName: 'openai',
    apiKey: '[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]',
    baseUrl: 'https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions',
    model: 'gpt-4o',
  ),
);
```

## Configuration

`LlmConfig.fromEnvironment()` resolves each value in order: the explicit
argument, then the `{PROVIDER}_…` environment variable, then the same name in
a project-root `.env` file, then the built-in default. `PROVIDER` is `OPENAI`
(the default), `OPENROUTER`, or `OLLAMA`.

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `{PROVIDER}_API_KEY` | API key |
| `{PROVIDER}_MODEL` | Model id |
| `{PROVIDER}_BASE_PATH` | Base URL — wins over `{PROVIDER}_BASE_URL` when both are set |
| `{PROVIDER}_BASE_URL` | Base URL (see below) |

A base URL may be an origin (`http://127.0.0.1:8931`), a versioned base
(`http://127.0.0.1:8931/v1`), or the full endpoint
(`https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions`); it is normalized to the full
chat-completions endpoint the providers POST to, so a local proxy (recorder,
gateway, cost tracker) can be pointed at with its origin alone.

## Features

- OpenAI-compatible streaming completions
- OpenRouter model routing
- Ollama local inference
- Provider configuration and resolution
- Token counting and context window management

- `LlmConfig.fromEnvironment(provider: 'copilot', baseUrl: <origin>)` now normalizes to `<origin>/v1/chat/completions` — which would break Copilot if `fromEnvironment` were used with copilot + explicit baseUrl. But `providerPrefix` for copilot maps to OPENAI... wait no, `providerPrefix` is used only for env key lookup. The provider itself is passed through as `resolvedProvider`.

So `LlmConfig.fromEnvironment(provider: 'copilot', baseUrl: 'https://api.githubcopilot.com')` returns baseUrl = `https://api.githubcopilot.com/v1/chat/completions`, and then `ProviderFactory.create` passes that to `copilotBaseUrl(baseUrlOverride: ...)` → CopilotProvider gets `https://api.githubcopilot.com/v1/chat/completions` as base, then appends `/chat/completions` → `https://api.githubcopilot.com/v1/chat/completions/chat/completions`. Broken.

But is copilot + fromEnvironment a realistic combination? `fromEnvironment` is a public API of the published package. The dartdoc added by this PR says "A base URL — an explicit `baseUrl` argument or a `{PROVIDER}_BASE_PATH` / `{PROVIDER}_BASE_URL` value — may be an origin..." and claims providers POST to "the full chat-completions endpoint". For copilot that's not true — CopilotProvider builds `baseUrl + path` itself. So the doc + normalization introduced a latent inconsistency for the `copilot` provider: the doc says the normalization applies to `LlmConfig.fromEnvironment` regardless of provider (well, it says PROVIDER is OPENAI, OPENROUTER, or OLLAMA — the doc explicitly scopes PROVIDER to those three).

But `fromEnvironment(provider: 'copilot')` still works and reads OPENAI_* vars. The normalization applies to copilot too since it's unconditional. That's a real edge case, but is it in scope? The `copilot` branch is reachable through `fromEnvironment` since provider: 'copilot' lowercases to 'copilot' and `resolvedProvider` is passed to the config. `ProviderFactory.create(config)` switches on `config.providerName` == 'copilot'.

So: `LlmConfig.fromEnvironment(provider: 'copilot', baseUrl: 'https://api.githubcopilot.com').baseUrl` → `'https://api.githubcopilot.com/v1/chat/completions'` → `ProviderFactory.create` → copilot branch → broken URL.

The docs scope PROVIDER to openai/openrouter/ollama, so arguably copilot users are told not to use fromEnvironment. But the code applies normalization unconditionally — the empty-value guard is the only exception. A provider-aware guard (skip copilot) would be safer. 4. **The `fullEndpoint` normalization semantics vs OpenAI SDK convention**: The PR says "the `OPENAI_BASE_URL` convention of the OpenAI SDKs". In the official OpenAI SDKs, `OPENAI_BASE_URL` is expected to include the version segment (e.g. `https://api.openai.com/v1`) — the SDK appends only `/chat/completions`. And notably, the OpenAI SDK convention does NOT append `/v1` when given an origin — actually, in the Python SDK, if base_url is set to an origin without `/v1`, requests go to `<origin>/chat/completions` (no `/v1`). Hmm, let me think.

In openai-python: `base_url = os.environ.get("OPENAI_BASE_URL", "https://api.openai.com/v1")` and then the client joins `/chat/completions`. So origin → `<origin>/chat/completions` (no /v1!). The PR's normalization maps origin → `<origin>/v1/chat/completions`. That differs from the OpenAI SDK convention for the origin case. But is that a problem? The PR's claim "as `OPENAI_BASE_URL` means in the OpenAI SDKs" is partially accurate: versioned base → same as SDK; full endpoint → different (SDK would produce `<base>/chat/completions` from a full endpoint — wait no: SDK given `https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions` as base_url would POST to `https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions/chat/completions`. So full-endpoint handling here is MORE forgiving than the SDK).

This is a docs-accuracy nit: the claim "as OPENAI_BASE_URL means in the OpenAI SDKs" is only partially true (origin case differs: SDK would give no `/v1`). Actually wait — for the origin case, which is more useful? For local gateways like LiteLLM (default `http://0.0.0.0:4000`), the OpenAI-compatible endpoint is `http://host:4000/v1/chat/completions`? No — LiteLLM proxy serves `/chat/completions` AND `/v1/chat/completions`? LiteLLM proxy serves `/v1/chat/completions`? Let me think. LiteLLM proxy: `curl http://0.0.0.0:4000/v1/chat/completions` — yes, `/v1` works, and also `/openai/v1`... Actually the LiteLLM proxy accepts both `/chat/completions` and `/v1/chat/completions`. The OpenAI SDK with base_url=`http://0.0.0.0:4000` would hit `http://0.0.0.0:4000/chat/completions` (no v1). So the chosen convention (origin → `/v1/chat/completions`) differs from the actual OpenAI SDK behavior. It matches what most people think happens. This is a minor docs nit — arguably SUGGESTION. But the claim in the dartdoc/README says "as `OPENAI_BASE_URL` means in the OpenAI SDKs" — this is the PR author's justification. Since the harness's own `defaultBaseUrl()` includes `/v1`, appending `/v1` for origins is self-consistent. I'll note it as a SUGGESTION-level docs precision point. Hmm, actually let me double check the OpenAI SDK behavior to be fair. In openai-python, the default base_url is "https://api.openai.com/v1/". If user sets OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434, then chat completions URL = http://localhost:11434/chat/completions. Yes, no /v1 appended. So the dartdoc claim is factually loose. SUGGESTION.

NEW behavior: POST to `https://gateway.example/api/v1/chat/completions`. This is a **breaking change for existing configs** that used custom path prefixes! The PR claims "Full-endpoint values pass through byte-identical (no behavior change for existing valid configs)" — that's only true for values that already ended in `/chat/completions` or `/v1`. A config with `OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://gateway.example/api` previously POSTed to exactly that URL; now it POSTs to `.../api/v1/chat/completions`.

## 0.2.0 — 2026-08-28

- GitHub Copilot as a first-class provider: OAuth device-flow auth (request/poll with pending/slow_down/expired/denied semantics), GitHub-token-to-Copilot-token exchange with dead-token detection, and login resolution.
- CopilotTokenManager: cached short-lived Copilot tokens with proactive refresh (2 min before expiry), 30 s minimum exchange spacing, single-flight locking, and forced refresh (getAgain) for 401/403 retries.
- CopilotTokenStore abstraction with an in-memory implementation for tests and apps without a secure backend.
- CopilotProvider over /chat/completions: streaming SSE and complete responses, mandatory Copilot headers, per-request X-Initiator and Copilot-Vision-Request, cancel that stops emission immediately, refresh-once retry on 401/403, and listModels() parsing capabilities/limits/supported_endpoints.
- ProviderFactory copilot branch with accountType (individual/business/enterprise), explicit baseUrl override, and entry-name-scoped token store wiring.
- LlmConfig gains optional accountType and entryName fields.

- OpenRouter provider with model routing.

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-29):
## Automated Code Review — COMMENT

**Summary**: The PR delivers what issue #1072 asked for — documented `{PROVIDER}_*` env overrides and forgiving base-URL normalization — and the ollama `…/v1/v1/…` double-append fix is real (verified: 16/16 targeted and 81/81 package tests pass, `dart analyze` clean). Three important issues remain: the normalizer is provider-blind and breaks the `ProviderFactory` copilot branch (which appends its own paths), verbatim query-string (Azure-style `?api-version=`) / custom-path base URLs that worked before now get `/v1/chat/completions` appended, and this published-package behavior change ships without the version bump + CHANGELOG entry the repo convention requires (cf. commit 54333f60).

**Next Steps**:
1. Exempt `copilot` from `fullEndpoint()` normalization (or gate it on providers that POST the fixed route) + regression test
2. Pass through URLs containing `?`/`#`, or match on `Uri.parse(url).path` instead of the raw string; add a query-string test
3. Bump `packages/fa_llm/pubspec.yaml` and add a CHANGELOG entry for the behavior change
4. Optional: pin the documented `BASE_PATH` > `BASE_URL` ordering with an injectable-env test, complete the README env-var table (4 of 8 variables), and soften the "as `OPENAI_BASE_URL` means in the OpenAI SDKs" dartdoc claim (SDKs do not insert `/v1` for a bare origin)

Notes outside the diff (no action required for this PR): the default endpoint URLs are duplicated between `LlmConfig.fromEnvironment`'s `defaultBaseUrl()` and `ProviderFactory._effectiveBaseUrl` — worth consolidating next time either changes; and `dotenv_loader.dart` does not strip quotes from `.env` values, which composes badly with any quoted `*_BASE_URL` value.

---


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-29):

🚨 **IMPORTANT: normalization is provider-blind — it breaks the `copilot` branch of `ProviderFactory`**

The comment claims "normalize every provider the same way", but `copilot` does not POST to a fixed `/chat/completions` route that the base URL should be normalized into:

- `ProviderFactory.create` (packages/fa_llm/lib/src/provider_factory.dart, `_createCopilot`) passes `config.baseUrl` verbatim as `baseUrlOverride` to `copilotBaseUrl()`.
- `CopilotProvider` builds its request URLs as `baseUrl + '/chat/completions'` (packages/fa_llm/lib/src/copilot/copilot_provider.dart:152), so its base must stay an origin (`https://api.githubcopilot.com`).

Consequence of this change:

```dart
LlmConfig.fromEnvironment(provider: 'copilot', baseUrl: 'https://api.githubcopilot.com').baseUrl
// → 'https://api.githubcopilot.com/v1/chat/completions'
// CopilotProvider then POSTs to:
// https://api.githubcopilot.com/v1/chat/completions/chat/completions
```

The new dartdoc scopes `PROVIDER` to openai/openrouter/ollama, but the code applies normalization unconditionally, and `fromEnvironment(provider: 'copilot')` is a supported public path (the factory has a copilot branch; `providerPrefix` even maps copilot's env lookups). No in-repo consumer hits this today (`toLlmConfig()` constructs `LlmConfig` directly), which is why this is not BLOCKING.

Suggested fix: exempt `copilot` from the rewrite, e.g.

```dart
if (resolvedProvider != 'copilot' && resolvedBaseUrl.isNotEmpty) {
  resolvedBaseUrl = fullEndpoint(resolvedBaseUrl);
}
```

plus a regression test pinning that a copilot base URL passes through untouched.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-29):

🚨 **IMPORTANT: aggressive append breaks previously-working verbatim base URLs (query strings, custom paths)**

Before this PR, `openai`/`openrouter` base URLs were used **verbatim** (only `ollama` was rewritten). Now any value not ending in `/chat/completions` or `/v1` gets `/v1/chat/completions` appended. Two realistic existing-config classes regress:

1. **Query-string endpoints (Azure native style)** — this worked verbatim before:
   ```
   https://myres.openai.azure.com/openai/deployments/gpt-4o/chat/completions?api-version=2024-10-21
   ```
   `endsWith('/chat/completions')` is false because the string ends with the query, so this PR turns it into
   `...chat/completions?api-version=2024-10-21/v1/chat/completions` — a 404 against a config that used to work.
2. **Custom-path gateways** not ending in `/v1` (previously POSTed-to exactly as configured) now silently get `/v1/chat/completions` appended.

The PR description's claim "no behavior change for existing valid configs" only holds for values ending in `/chat/completions` or `/v1`.

Cheap hardening that keeps the documented forgiving semantics:

```dart
String fullEndpoint(String url) {
  if (url.contains('?') || url.contains('#')) return url; // full URL with query/fragment: pass through
  final base = url.replaceAll(RegExp(r'/+$'), '');
  ...
}
```

(or parse with `Uri.parse` and match on `path` instead of the raw string). At minimum, add a test documenting the chosen behavior for a query-string value.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-29):

🚨 **IMPORTANT: published-package behavior change without version bump or CHANGELOG entry**

This line changes the observable output of the public `LlmConfig.fromEnvironment` factory for every provider (normalization now applies to openai/openrouter too, not just ollama). `fa_llm` is published to pub.dev (`.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` publishes on `fa_llm-v*` tags), and the repo convention for `fa_llm` behavior/feature changes is to ship both together — see commit 54333f60, which bumped `pubspec.yaml` 0.1.0 → 0.2.0 and added the CHANGELOG section in the same commit.

This PR modifies behavior but touches neither:

- `packages/fa_llm/pubspec.yaml` — still `version: 0.2.0`
- `packages/fa_llm/CHANGELOG.md` — newest entry still `## 0.2.0 — 2026-08-28`

Without them, a future `fa_llm-v0.2.x` tag would republish the package with identical version metadata but different `fromEnvironment` behavior. Please bump (0.2.1 is fine — arguably 0.3.0 given the query-string pass-through regression risk in the sibling comment) and add a CHANGELOG entry describing the new accepted base-URL shapes.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-29):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the "as `OPENAI_BASE_URL` means in the OpenAI SDKs" claim is only partially accurate**

In the official OpenAI SDKs, `OPENAI_BASE_URL` is a **versioned base** and the SDK appends only `/chat/completions`; a bare origin yields `<origin>/chat/completions` (no `/v1` is inserted). This normalizer instead maps an origin to `<origin>/v1/chat/completions`.

That convention choice is fine (it matches vLLM/LiteLLM-style servers and the package's own defaults, which all carry `/v1`), but the doc sentence over-claims equivalence. Suggest wording like:

```dart
/// … so a local proxy can be pointed at with its origin alone — a
/// superset of the `OPENAI_BASE_URL` versioned-base convention in the
/// OpenAI SDKs.
```

so users porting a literal origin-shaped `OPENAI_BASE_URL` from an SDK setup are not surprised by the inserted `/v1`.

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-29):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the env-var table the issue asked for lists only 4 of the 8 documented variables**

The `LlmConfig` dartdoc added in this PR enumerates eight variables: `{PROVIDER}_API_KEY`, `_MODEL`, `_BASE_PATH`, `_BASE_URL`, `_MAX_TOKENS`, `_CONTEXT_WINDOW`, `_TEMPERATURE`, `_MAX_TOKENS_PARAM_NAME`. The truncated diff actually covers nearly everything (only ~31 chars omitted in the middle — the pubspec repository/homepage lines). Let me now verify against the actual git diff for completeness, then deep-review the new `fullEndpoint` implementation.

New `fullEndpoint`:
```dart
String fullEndpoint(String url) {
  final uri = Uri.tryParse(url);
  if (uri == null || uri.hasQuery || uri.hasFragment) return url;
  final base = url.replaceAll(RegExp(r'/+$'), '');
  if (base.endsWith('/chat/completions')) return base;
  if (base.endsWith('/v1')) return '$base/chat/completions';
  if (uri.path.isEmpty || uri.path == '/') {
    return '$base/v1/chat/completions';
  }
  return url;
}
```

Analysis of the new logic:

1. `Uri.tryParse(url)` null → return url verbatim. Good.
2. `uri.hasQuery || uri.hasFragment` → verbatim. Good (fixes Azure).
3. Trailing-slash strip.
4. `/chat/completions` → pass. Good.
5. `/v1` → append route. Good.
6. **NEW**: if `uri.path.isEmpty || uri.path == '/'` → append `/v1/chat/completions` (origin case). 
7. **Otherwise (custom path)** → `return url` verbatim.

Wait — there are subtle issues here:

**Issue A: trailing-slash stripping no longer applied in the verbatim branches.** If url = `'https://gw.example/corp-route/'` (custom path with trailing slash) → not origin (path = `/corp-route/`), not `/v1`, not `/chat/completions` → `return url` — WITH the trailing slash, verbatim. That's fine per "passes through verbatim".

But `'https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions///'`? → base strips trailing slashes → endsWith `/chat/completions` → returns STRIPPED base `'https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions'`. OK — normalized (slash strip). The doc says full endpoints "pass through verbatim" — with trailing slashes they're normalized. Minor; the test only covers `.../v1/`. Fine, that's the previous behavior, consistent.

**Issue B: `'http://127.0.0.1:8931'` (origin) — `uri.path`**: For `'http://127.0.0.1:8931'`, `Uri.parse` gives `path == ''` → origin branch → append. Good. For `'http://127.0.0.1:8931/'` → path == '/' → append. Good — trailing slashes stripped by `base` first, then append: `'http://127.0.0.1:8931' + '/v1/chat/completions'`. Good.

**Issue C: What about `uri.path` for URLs with a port but empty host? Not realistic.

**Issue D: IPv6**: `'http://[::1]:11434'` — Uri.tryParse handles brackets; path '' → append → `'http://[::1]:11434/v1/chat/completions'`. Good.

**Issue E: The custom-path verbatim return changed semantics vs my round-1 suggestion**: my suggested "custom-path gateways now silently get /v1/chat/completions appended" — the author chose verbatim pass-through for custom paths. That's the SAFEST choice (byte-identical to pre-PR behavior for openai/openrouter). 

**Issue F — regression re-introduced? `ollama` custom-path**: pre-PR, ollama rewrote EVERYTHING non-full-endpoint (append `/v1/chat/completions`); post-PR, ollama custom paths pass verbatim. That's a behavior change for ollama custom-path configs — but it's the fix direction the issue asked for and matches openai. Fine.

**Issue G — `/v1` check happens BEFORE the path check**: url `'https://gw.example/corp-route/v1'` → endsWith `/v1` → `'https://gw.example/corp-route/v1/chat/completions'`. Hmm — is that right? A custom path ending in `/v1` gains the route. That's the "versioned base" semantics — any path ending `/v1` is treated as versioned base. Reasonable and consistent with docs ("a versioned base (`http://127.0.0.1:8931/v1`)"). Fine.

**Issue H — UPPERCASE `/V1`?** Case-sensitive; fine.

**Issue J — what does `uri.hasQuery` do for `'http://h?'`?** hasQuery true (empty query) → verbatim. Fine.

**Issue K — Uri.tryParse leniency**: `'not a url'` → Uri.tryParse succeeds (relative reference), path = 'not a url', not empty → verbatim. Good — garbage passes through (will fail at request time as before).

**Issue L — `'http://host/v1/chat/completions/'`**: strip → endsWith → stripped base. Good.

**Issue M — `uri.path.isEmpty` can never be true together with... hmm, for `'https://host'` path is ''. For `'https://host/'` path is '/'. Both covered.

The default branch maps unknown provider names → OpenAiProvider. So an unknown provider name 'foo' → OPENAI dialect normalization → OpenAiProvider posts to full URL. Consistent. Good.
